Question B-003-018-001.

Why the correct answer is right: A key-operated switch positively controls station power, making casual or unauthorized home operation much harder.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "Use a key-operated on/off switch in the main power line": This is the correct choice because a key-operated switch positively controls station power, making casual or unauthorized home operation much harder.
- sourceIndex 1: "Use a carrier-operated relay in the main power line": This is a near-miss because it shifts attention from Use a key-operated on/off switch in the main power line. In station access, shock hazards, high-voltage rescue, and safe de-energizing before work, power alone is not the control or safety mechanism being tested in this item.
- sourceIndex 2: "Put a \"Danger - High Voltage\" sign in the station": This answer would fit a different fault than Use a key-operated on/off switch in the main power line. In station access, shock hazards, high-voltage rescue, and safe de-energizing before work, this misreads the voltage relationship or protection rating involved in the question.
- sourceIndex 3: "Put fuses in the main power line": This option confuses another station topic with Use a key-operated on/off switch in the main power line. In station access, shock hazards, high-voltage rescue, and safe de-energizing before work, power alone is not the control or safety mechanism being tested in this item.
